title: A Semiclassical Gaussian Wavepacket Method for Non-Adiabatic Molecular Dynamics
authors: Lorenzo Bocchi, Jia-Xi Zeng, Michele Ceotto
abstract: We introduce two non-adiabatic semiclassical methods that employ two coupled Gaussian wavepackets, each one traveling on a separate diabatic potential energy surface. The wavepackets take the form of thawed Gaussians and are driven by classical equations of motion which account for the diabatic coupling. The classical equations of motion are derived in one case by enforcing the thawed Gaussian ansatz, while in the other the time-dependent variational principles to the thawed Gaussian ansatz. After a sanity check where both approximations reproduce Rabi oscillations, the methods are applied to two non-adiabatic potential energy scenarios. The first one involves two coupled displaced harmonic oscillators, as in a typical electron transfer reaction. The second one comprises a Morse potential coupled to an upper dissociative state, modeling a photo-dissociation process. In both scenarios, the variational thawed Gaussian approach is quite accurate, while the standard thawed Gaussian one fails to fully capture the non-adiabatic effects. Ultimately, non-adiabatic molecular dynamics is reproduced by means of two classical trajectories without introducing any artificial jump or other ad-hoc non-classical effects.
summary: This paper introduces advanced semiclassical Gaussian wavepacket methods to simulate complex non-adiabatic molecular dynamics. The authors propose an improved variational approach (NA-VTGWD) which correctly models electronic state transitions by coupling classical trajectories on diabatic surfaces. This method proves superior to standard approximations, accurately reproducing quantum effects in systems like electron transfer and photo-dissociation.
main_problem: The primary challenge is accurately simulating non-adiabatic molecular dynamics, which requires methods beyond the Born-Oppenheimer approximation.
main_result: The proposed Variational Thawed Gaussian method (NA-VTGWD) successfully reproduces quantum mechanical results for various non-adiabatic processes while maintaining crucial physical symmetries like energy and norm conservation.
method: The authors develop two semiclassical methods based on the thawed Gaussian ansatz: a standard formulation (NA-TGWD) and an improved variational version (NA-VTGWD) derived from time-dependent variational principles.
model_or_system: The models involve coupled electronic states described by diabatic potential energy surfaces ($V_{11}, V_{22}$) with coupling terms ($V_{12}$). Tests include electron transfer using coupled harmonic oscillators and photo-dissociation modeled with a Morse potential.
key_observables: Diabatic state populations ($ho_{ii}(t)$), wavepacket density heatmaps, and conservation of total energy and norm.
important_parameters: The coupling strength ($V_{12}$), the nature of the potentials (harmonic vs. Morse), and the time evolution parameters for the Gaussian wavepackets.
main_assumptions: Both methods rely on the thawed Gaussian ansatz, which is exact only for specific potential forms; the variational approach is superior because it guarantees adherence to the Schrödinger equation solution.
figures_summary: Figures compare population dynamics and wavepacket heatmaps across three approaches: exact quantum evolution (split-operator), NA-VTGWD, and the less accurate NA-TGWD for both coupled oscillators and Morse potential systems.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the general problem, details the two semiclassical methods (NA-TGWD in one section, NA-VTGWD in another), validates them using Rabi oscillations, and applies them to complex physical scenarios like electron transfer and photo-dissociation.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses non-adiabatic dynamics—a cornerstone of molecular physics and quantum chemistry—by providing a computationally tractable semiclassical framework that rigorously conserves fundamental quantities.
